regional_assessment: Southern Hemisphere subtropical/semi-arid maize systems exhibit strong summer rainfall deficits with high evaporative demand. Calibration data (2004-2016) reveals robust negative residual associations between yield and extreme heat (tmin<5°C, tmax>31.6°C) and severe precipitation scarcity (prec<0.37mm). The yield distribution is heavily skewed left (median 5.06 t/ha vs mean 5.68 t/ha), indicating frequent low-yield events driven by moisture stress and cold snaps. Feature selection must prioritize thermal stress accumulation (GDD) and antecedent soil moisture deficits to capture the directionally stable yield penalties observed.

candidates.agronomic_rationale: Targets the statistically significant negative yield residuals associated with minimum temperatures below 5°C. In semi-arid summer-rainfall zones, nocturnal cooling below this threshold can induce chilling stress during critical reproductive stages or reduce diurnal temperature range needed for VPD-driven transpiration. This feature captures the frequency/duration of events where tmin < 5°C to quantify thermal stress accumulation.

Captures the persistent negative yield impact of maximum temperatures exceeding 31.6°C, identified as the 90th percentile threshold with significant residual correlation. High tmax in semi-arid regions accelerates crop senescence and increases vapor pressure deficit beyond plant tolerance, leading to the observed yield penalties. This feature aggregates days where tmax > 31.6°C to measure heat stress exposure.

Leverages the strongest negative residual signal (r=-0.345) associated with precipitation falling below 0.37 mm/day. Given the semi-arid context and high evaporative demand, days with negligible rainfall (<0.37mm) represent critical soil moisture depletion events that drive the left-skewed yield distribution. This feature counts days where daily precipitation is strictly less than the 25th percentile to quantify moisture stress frequency.
